samples.summary: New read walk guards a negative block index; the matching write path (`Doc.applyInlineStyle`) still does not, so the same range crashes on write
samples.evidence: `visitStyledRunsInRange` (range-runs.ts:159-161) does `const anchorIdx = doc.getBlockIndex(anchorTopId); ... if (anchorIdx < 0 || focusIdx < 0) return;` and also `if (!block) continue;` at line 172. The write path it is explicitly mirroring has neither guard: document.ts:395-411 computes `startBlock`/`endBlock` from `getBlockIndex` (which returns -1 when the normalized top id is not in the current context — e.g. an endpoint inside a *nested* table cell, whose `blockParentMap` entry points at the inner table block that is not a context block, or a cell block whose parent-map entry is missing because layout has not run since the table was inserted), then loops `for (let i = fromBlockIdx; i <= toBlockIdx; i++) { const block = contextBlocks[i]; ... if (block.type === 'table' ...)` — with i === -1 `block` is `undefined` and `block.type` throws a TypeError. Because the toolbar/keyboard now derive an *empty* summary for exactly these ranges (the read returns early), a toggle still calls `applyStyle`/`toggleStyle` on that range and reaches the unguarded write. The read-side guard makes the divergence silent instead of surfacing it.

samples.summary: Text-box `getRangeStyleSummary` now reports effective (named-style-layered) font size, but `stepSelectionFontSize` in the same file still steps from the raw run size — read and write disagree
samples.evidence: The diff changed the summary in this file to `visitStyledRunsInRange(doc, range, (effective) => ...)`, which reports `{...resolveStyleInline(blockStyleId(block)), ...inline.style}` (range-runs.ts:56-68). The stepper immediately above was not changed: text-box-editor.ts:887 still does `const size = inline.style.fontSize ?? DEFAULT_INLINE_STYLE.fontSize ?? 11;`. For a block whose named style supplies the size (title → 26, heading-1 → 20) and whose run carries no explicit `fontSize`, the picker now displays 26 while pressing `+` steps 11 → 12 — the picker jumps backwards. This is the same read/write asymmetry the PR sets out to remove, left in place for the text-box stepper.

samples.summary: Text-box summary's collapsed-caret branch still returns raw `inline.style`, so the #715 'style comes from the named style' case is only fixed for ranges, not for a caret
samples.evidence: text-box-editor.ts:1024-1041 returns `{ ...inline.style, ...staged }` with no `resolveStyleInline` layer, while the range branch (line 1076) now layers named-style defaults. In a text-box block whose named style supplies italic (e.g. heading-6), a collapsed caret makes `getRangeStyleSummary().italic` undefined → `isStyleOn` false → the toolbar renders the button unpressed and the first click applies `italic: true`, a visual no-op. The docs editor's equivalent branch (editor.ts:2707-2723) does layer the defaults, so the two surfaces disagree.

samples.summary: `stepSelectionFontSize` now resizes the entire text of any table merely crossed by a selection, which it previously skipped
samples.evidence: The old collect pass called `collectRunsInBlock(block.id, from, to)` on context blocks; a table block has no inlines, so tables caught in a cross-block selection contributed no runs and were never resized. `visitStyledRunsInRange` adds `if (block.type === 'table' && block.tableData) { visitTable(block); continue; }` (range-runs.ts:175-178), so every run in every cell of such a table is now collected and written by `docStore.applyStyles`. This is consistent with `Doc.applyInlineStyle`, so it may be intended, but it is an unannounced behavioural change to the font +/- control (selecting a paragraph before and after a table now rescales the whole table) and no test in the diff covers it.

finding.summary: New read walk guards a negative block index; the matching write path (`Doc.applyInlineStyle`) still does not, so the same range crashes on write
finding.evidence: `visitStyledRunsInRange` (range-runs.ts:159-161) does `const anchorIdx = doc.getBlockIndex(anchorTopId); ... if (anchorIdx < 0 || focusIdx < 0) return;` and also `if (!block) continue;` at line 172. The write path it is explicitly mirroring has neither guard: document.ts:395-411 computes `startBlock`/`endBlock` from `getBlockIndex` (which returns -1 when the normalized top id is not in the current context — e.g. an endpoint inside a *nested* table cell, whose `blockParentMap` entry points at the inner table block that is not a context block, or a cell block whose parent-map entry is missing because layout has not run since the table was inserted), then loops `for (let i = fromBlockIdx; i <= toBlockIdx; i++) { const block = contextBlocks[i]; ... if (block.type === 'table' ...)` — with i === -1 `block` is `undefined` and `block.type` throws a TypeError. Because the toolbar/keyboard now derive an *empty* summary for exactly these ranges (the read returns early), a toggle still calls `applyStyle`/`toggleStyle` on that range and reaches the unguarded write. The read-side guard makes the divergence silent instead of surfacing it.

verdict.reason: Verified as described. range-runs.ts:159-161 guards `anchorIdx/focusIdx < 0` and :172 guards `!block`, while the mirrored write walk in document.ts:395-415 does neither: `getBlockIndex` (document.ts:210-211) is a findIndex over `getContextBlocks()` and returns -1 when the normalized top id is not a context block — true for a nested table, whose id is what `_blockParentMap` yields for a nested cell block. With fromBlockIdx === -1 the loop still runs and `contextBlocks[-1]` is undefined, so `block.type` at document.ts:415 throws a TypeError. Reachable without any guard: caret in a nested cell + Shift+Down exits into the outer cell (text-editor.ts:2614-2648), and because the endpoints' tableBlockIds differ the tableCellRange branch at text-editor.ts:2660-2663 is skipped and a plain range is set at :2683; Cmd+B (:871-875) reaches toggleStyle, passes the tableCellRange check at :2924, and calls doc.applyInlineStyle at :2931 with no try/catch. editor.ts:1051 is a second unguarded caller. That the very next lines (text-editor.ts:2935, editor.ts:1061-1063) explicitly handle negative indices for markDirty shows the -1 case is anticipated everywhere except the write walk. Crash on a real user path in the correctness lane.

finding.summary: Read walk recurses into nested tables; the write (`Doc.applyInlineStyle`) does not — reintroducing the #715 "can only add, never remove" trap for selections spanning a table that contains a nested table
finding.evidence: `visitTable` (range-runs.ts:68-83) recurses: `if (cellBlock.type === 'table' && cellBlock.tableData) visitTable(cellBlock)`. The write it claims to mirror does not: `Doc.applyInlineStyle` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:415-429) iterates `cell.blocks` and calls `store.applyStyle(cellBlock.id, 0, len)` only when `len = getBlockTextLength(cellBlock) > 0`; a nested table block has `inlines: []` so `len === 0` and its inner cell blocks are never styled. Consequence: for a cross-block selection covering a table whose nested table content differs (e.g. outer runs bold, nested runs not), the read reports `allOn === false` / `'mixed'` forever, so both `isStyleOnInSelection` (text-editor.ts:3007) and the toolbar's `isStyleOn` always resolve to "apply", the write never touches the nested runs, and the style can never be removed — exactly the failure mode this change set out to fix. The `tableCellRange` branch (range-runs.ts:98) is consistent with the write because it uses `visitWholeBlock` (0 runs for a table block); only `visitTable` diverges.

verdict.reason: The finding's central evidence is not in the repository. It quotes `visitTable` as recursing: `if (cellBlock.type === 'table' && cellBlock.tableData) visitTable(cellBlock)`. The only definition of `visitTable` (packages/docs/src/view/range-runs.ts:78-94) contains no recursive call — its cell loop body is exactly `for (const cellBlock of cell.blocks) visitWholeBlock(cellBlock);`, preceded by a comment ("Deliberately *not* recursive") that rejects recursion for the very #715 reason the finding cites as the consequence. Grep for `visitTable` shows one definition (range-runs.ts:78) and one call site (range-runs.ts:176), so no alternate recursive copy exists. Furthermore, the read/write symmetry the finding says is broken actually holds: the write (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:420-425) skips a cell block when `getBlockTextLength(cellBlock) === 0`, and the read's `visitWholeBlock` (range-runs.ts:75-76) calls `visitBlockSlice(block.id, 0, 0)` for a table block, where the overlap condition `pos < to` at range-runs.ts:61 is false for every inline, visiting nothing. `getBlockTextLength` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:326-328) reduces over `block.inlines`, empty for a table block, so both read and write compute 0 and both skip nested tables. No runs enter the read set that the write cannot restyle, so the alleged "mixed forever / can only add, never remove" failure mode cannot arise from this code.

finding.summary: Collapsed-caret keyboard toggle still reads the RAW run style (no named-style defaults), so Cmd+I in a heading whose named style supplies italic remains a permanent visual no-op and disagrees with the toolbar
finding.evidence: `toggleStyle` falls back to `!!visual[key]` when `isStyleOnInSelection` returns `undefined`, which is exactly the collapsed-caret case. `visual` comes from `getStyleAtCursor()` (text-editor.ts:2974-2988), which returns `{...inline.style}` only — no `resolveStyleInline` defaults. So with a caret inside a Heading 6 (built-in style sets italic) Cmd+I computes `!false` → writes pending `italic: true`, a no-op the user can never undo from the keyboard. The docs toolbar in the same situation reads `getRangeStyleSummary()`, whose collapsed path DOES layer defaults (editor.ts:2787-2803, 2812) and therefore writes `italic: false`. The keyboard/toolbar disagreement the change claims to end still exists for collapsed carets.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is not present. The collapsed-caret fallback in `toggleStyle` reads `effectiveVisual`, not the raw `visual`: text-editor.ts:2898 builds `const effectiveVisual = { ...this.styleDefaultsAtCursor(), ...visual }` and text-editor.ts:2906-2908 computes `!(inRange ?? !!effectiveVisual[key])`. `styleDefaultsAtCursor()` (text-editor.ts:3006-3010) returns `resolveStyleInline(blockStyleId(block), this.doc.document.styles)`, which for a Heading 6 yields `italic: true` (named-styles.ts:91, resolution at named-styles.ts:119-127, id mapping at named-styles.ts:99-114). So for the finding's exact scenario — caret in Heading 6, `isStyleOnInSelection` returns `undefined` (text-editor.ts:3029-3031) — the fallback is `!!true`, so `resolved.italic = false` and pending is set to italic:false (text-editor.ts:2918), which is the same verdict the finding attributes to the toolbar. No permanent no-op and no keyboard/toolbar disagreement exists on this path. The raw `visual` is used only for what is *stored* in pending (intentional, per the comment at 2890-2897), which does not affect the add-vs-remove decision the finding describes.
